professional_summary.short_bio: Game audio designer. Wwise, C++, Unreal Engine.
professional_summary.extended_bio: I have a background in classical piano, but I never felt at home just performing. I needed to know *how* the sound worked. That curiosity pushed me from music school into physics and math, and eventually to Game Audio. Now, I don't just design sounds; I write the C++ and Python tools to make them run effectively in real-time.
professional_summary.philosophy: A gunshot that sounds amazing but causes a frame drop is a bad sound. Audio has to work within CPU and memory budgets.

clarity_first.title: Mix Hierarchy
clarity_first.description: In *Shadow Frames*, we had a problem: the ambient pub noise was drowning out the enemy footsteps. Instead of just turning it down, I built a sidechain system that ducks the environment specifically when an enemy is moving. The threat always cuts through.

technical_limits.title: Budgets & Constraints
technical_limits.description: For *Not Today Darling*, we hit a wall: 4-player shared-screen on a budget. The voice count was skyrocketing. I had to be ruthless—aggressive priority culling and forcing mono on anything that wasn't critical. We shipped a clean mix that ran smoothly.

layering_parameters.title: Parametric Sound Design
layering_parameters.description: I hate repeating work. Instead of making 20 unique engine sounds, I built one MetaSound graph that morphs based on speed and RPM. It covers walking, running, and sprinting without needing unique assets for every state.

collaboration.title: Playtest-Driven Audio
collaboration.description: Designers shouldn't have to ask me to change a volume slider. In *Shadow Frames*, I exposed all the key audio variables as DataAssets. Now the team tweaks tension curves and footstep volumes in the editor, and I can focus on the code.

featured_projects.title: Transientica: AudioLab
featured_projects.tagline: ML-powered beatbox recognition for rhythm gaming
featured_projects.short_description: Control a rhythm game using only your voice. Real-time beatbox recognition with <60ms latency.
featured_projects.detailed_description: Voice-controlled rhythm game using ML beatbox recognition. 92% accurate (tested on 450 samples), 45-60ms latency. Train the system with 30 examples of each drum sound. Python/scikit-learn ML, Unity game engine.

technical_achievements.pipeline: Spectral-flux for onset detection, SVM for classification
technical_achievements.optimization: Smaller FFT window (512 samples, 11ms), circular buffer eliminates I/O blocking, lightweight SVM (2ms vs 15ms neural net)
technical_achievements.architecture: Separated audio and ML threads, lock-free ringbuffer, audio on high priority thread

challenges_solved.problem: First version had 180ms lag - too slow for rhythm games
challenges_solved.solution: Optimized pipeline: smaller FFT window, circular buffer, lightweight SVM, UDP for OSC. Got to 45ms with 92% accuracy

challenges_solved.problem: Both have transients and noise - lots of wrong guesses
challenges_solved.solution: Added spectral centroid, zero-crossing rate, envelope shape features. Separate models for solo vs patterns. 78% to 92% accuracy

challenges_solved.problem: Heavy ML caused buffer underruns on weak CPUs
challenges_solved.solution: Separated threads with lock-free ringbuffer. Audio never blocks, ML on worker thread

featured_projects.full_description:
Real-time beatbox recognition system. Control rhythm games with your voice.

Optimized audio buffers and ML pipeline to stay under 60ms latency. Python handles audio analysis, Unity handles gameplay - communication via UDP/OSC.

code_snippets.title: Real-time Inference Loop (Python)
code_snippets.description: Audio buffer processing and SVM classification.
code_snippets.code:
def audio_callback(indata, frames, time, status):
    if status:
        print(status)
    
    # Add new data to ring buffer
    ring_buffer.extend(indata[:, 0])
    
    # Extract features
    features = extract_features(list(ring_buffer)[-BUFFER_SIZE:])
    
    # Predict
    prediction = model.predict([features])[0]
    
    # Send OSC if confidence high
    if prediction != 'silence':
        client.send_message("/beatbox/trigger", prediction)

code_snippets.title: Clean & Rebuild Logic (Batch)
code_snippets.description: Automates the deletion of intermediate/derived data caches to force a clean engine rebuild.
code_snippets.code:
@echo off
echo Cleaning Unreal Engine Intermediate Files...

RMDIR /S /Q "Intermediate"
RMDIR /S /Q "Binaries"
RMDIR /S /Q "DerivedDataCache"
RMDIR /S /Q "Saved"

echo Regenerating Project Files...
"%UE5_ENGINE_PATH%\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat" -project="%PROJECT_PATH%" -progress

echo Build Complete.
pause
